title: Discover safely generatable operation patterns
purpose: Expose an evidence-bounded inventory of operation patterns whose prerequisites determine whether the CLI may generate them, and execute an explicitly declared local provider only after its action, effect, binding and request envelope close.
policies: Availability is derived from explicit prerequisites and never from a pattern name.
A pattern is generatable only when its meta-type, binding, generator and conformance prerequisites are closed.
Registration creates a candidate; stable maturity requires a separate owner decision.
Blocked patterns remain visible with causal blockers and generate no implementation code.
An explicit effect and performs edge is required before an implementation generator may run.
Provider-specific generators must bind a concrete integration manifest and executable conformance evidence.
Runtime provider selection requires the exact action performs edge and matching effect binding; a pattern name never selects a provider.
Runtime infrastructure values are supplied in an explicit effect request and never inferred from fact names.
Committing an Outbox message and dispatching it are separate explicit operations.
Dispatch ownership is represented by expiring leases; failed delivery follows an explicit bounded retry and dead-letter policy.
HTTP dispatch requires an exact allowlisted origin and a matching operator confirmation; message identity is carried as the idempotency key.
Consumer idempotency is represented by an inbox receipt committed atomically with the local consumer mutation.
Provider runtime observations emit bounded telemetry without changing domain decisions.
exclusions: Code generation from an unregistered effect name
claim_ceiling: Candidate discovery, generation and local SQLite execution capability; local evidence does not admit the pattern, make it stable, authorize network effects, or prove production readiness.
